items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public authorities law and the county law, in relation to
authorizing the dormitory authority to construct and finance regional juvenile
detention facilities; and to designate certain non-profit corporations as the
agency of county government responsible for the administration of county
juvenile detention programs
items.lawCode: Amd §§1676 & 1680, Pub Auth L; amd §218-a, County L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8808

SPONSOR: TEDISCO
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the public authorities law and the
county law, in relation to authorizing the dormitory authority to
construct and finance regional juvenile detention facilities; and to
designate certain non-profit corporations as the agency of county
government responsible for the administration of county juvenile
detention programs

 
PURPOSE:

To authorize the Dormitory Authority to construct and finance regional
juvenile detention facilities and to allow counties to designate certain
nonprofit corporations as an agency of county government responsible for
the administration of county juvenile detention programs.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Amends paragraph (b) of subdivision 2 of section 1676 of the
public authorities law to amend the definition of "dormitory" to include
not-for-profit corporations formed pursuant to an inter-municipal agree-
ment among two or more counties within the state to assist the forming
counties with financing, constructing and operating a regional juvenile
detention center.

Section 2. Amends subdivision 1 of section 1680 of the public authori-
ties law to amend the definition of "educational institution" to include
not-for-profit corporations formed pursuant to an inter-municipal agree-
ment among two or more counties within the state to assist the forming
counties with financing, constructing and operating a regional juvenile
detention center.

Section 3. Amends subdivision 2 of section 1680 of the public authori-
ties law to authorize the Dormitory Authority to enter into agreements
with such not-for-profit corporations formed pursuant to an inter-muni-
cipal agreement among two or more counties to finance and construct
regional juvenile detention programs.

Section 4. Amends subdivision a of section 218-a of the county law to
allow counties to designate such not-for-profit corporations formed
pursuant to an inter-municipal agreement among two or more counties to
be an agency of county government responsible for the administration of
county juvenile detention programs

Section 5. Effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This bill would enable not-for-profit corporations, formed pursuant to
inter-municipal agreements to provide for county juvenile detention
programs, to access the services of the Dormitory Authority in order to
finance and construct specialized secured detention facilities required
by the recently enacted legislation that raised the age of juvenile
jurisdiction to include 16 and 17 year olds, commonly known as the Raise
the Age. In addition, the bill would clarify that counties can designate
such non-for-profit corporations as an agency of county government
responsible for the administration of county juvenile detention
programs. This clarification would enable such not-for-profit corpo-
rations direct access to the Raise the Age reimbursement funding
provided in the 2018-19 New York State budget.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8808A

SPONSOR: TEDISCO
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the public authorities law, in
relation to authorizing the dormitory authority to construct and finance
regional juvenile detention facilities

 
PURPOSE:

To authorize the Dormitory Authority to construct and finance regional
juvenile detention facilities and to allow counties to designate certain
non-profit corporations as an agency of county government responsible
for the administration of county juvenile detention programs.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Amends paragraph (b) of subdivision 2 of section 1676 of the
public authorities law to amend the definition of "dormitory" to include
not-for-profit corporations formed pursuant to an inter-municipal agree-
ment among two or more counties within the state to assist the forming
counties with financing, constructing, or otherwise disposing of a joint
county juvenile detention center established in accordance with section
two hundred eighteen-a of the county law.

Section 2. Amends subdivision 1 of section 1680 of the public authori-
ties law to amend the definition of "educational institution" to include
not-for-profit corporations formed pursuant to an inter-municipal agree-
ment among two or more counties within the state to assist the forming
counties with financing, constructing or otherwise disposing of a joint
county juvenile detention center established in accordance with section
two hundred eighteen-a of the county law.

Section 3. Amends subdivision 2 of section 1680 of the public authori-
ties law to authorize the Dormitory Authority to enter into agreements
with such not-for-profit corporations formed pursuant to an inter-muni-
cipal agreement among two or more counties to finance and construct
regional juvenile detention programs established in accordance with
section two hundred eighteen-a of the county law, or for the provision
of residential facilities licensed by the office of children and family
services including all necessary and usual attendant and related facili-
ties and equipment.

Section 4. Amends subdivision a of section 218-a of the county law to
allow counties to designate such not-for-profit corporations formed
pursuant to an inter-municipal agreement among two or more counties to
be an agency of county government responsible for the administration of
county juvenile detention programs

Section 5. Effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This bill would enable not-for-profit corporations, formed pursuant to
inter-municipal agreements to provide for county juvenile detention
programs, to access the services of the Dormitory Authority in order to
finance and construct specialized secured detention facilities required
by the recently enacted legislation that raised the age of juvenile
jurisdiction to include 16 and 17 year olds, commonly known as the Raise
the Age. In addition, the bill would clarify that counties can designate
such non-for-profit corporations as an agency of county government
responsible for the administration of county juvenile detention
programs. This clarification would enable such not-for-profit corpo-
rations direct access to the Raise the Age reimbursement funding
provided in the 2018-19 New York State budget.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
